Kamchatka Peninsula
Peninsula in Eastern Russia between the Pacific Ocean and the Sea of OkhotskThe Kamchatka Peninsula is a 1,250-kilometre-long peninsula in the Russian Far East, with an area of about 270,000 km². The Sea of Okhotsk bounds the peninsula's western coastline, immediately offshore of the peninsula and below the Bering Sea runs the 9,600-metre-deep Kuril–Kamchatka Trench. Its eastern coastline is the Bering Sea, part of the Pacific Ocean. The Kamchatka Peninsula, the Commander Islands, and Karaginsky Island constitute Kamchatka Krai of the Russian Federation. The majority of the 322,079 inhabitants are ethnic Russians, with about 13,000 being Koryaks. WikipediaLocation
